newsitem.title: CYPRUS: U.S. senator warns Bow Valley on Iranian field-MEE.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator warns Bow Valley on Iranian field-MEE.

text.p: United States Senator Alfonse D'Amato has warned Canadian firm Bow Valley Energy against signing a deal with Iran for development of the offshore Balal oil field, the Middle East Economic Survey reported on Monday.

The newsletter said D'Amato had told Bow Valley that "deals such as this violate the letter, as well as the spirit, of the Iran-Libya Sanctions Act" and warned that "if you go forward with it, however, you will join Total SA of France as a pariah company known for supporting rogue states".
MEES said a similar letter had been sent to Britain's Frischmann Group.
MEES said Bow Valley, in a joint venture with the Pell Frischmann Group, had bid for the development of Balal and is currently negotiating with National Iranian Oil Co executives (NIOC).

MEES said Bow Valley and Pell Frischmann's $212 million bid on the 40,000 barrels per day field was approved by NIOC in May. Final contract signature was contingent on the finalisation of financing arrangements.
"A number of other firms are waiting in the wings to replace Pell Frischmann/Bow Valley if the joint venture fails to secure the necessary financing to support the project," MEES said.

D'Amato sponsored the Iran-Libya Sanctions Act, under which companies investing more than $40 million in any one year in Iranian and Libyan oil and gas projects could be subject to a range of trade and financial penalties.
So far, the United States has not penalised any firms under the August 1996 law.
Total became the first foreign oil firm to secure a stake in an Iranian oilfield since Iran's 1979 revolution when it signed a $600 million deal in July 1995 to develop Iran's Sirri fields.
